name: Ashwall Fixer's Complete Underworld Set
description: A fixer's look is studied neutrality: mid-weight longcoat in slate-grey waxed synthwool, unbranded, cut wide enough to conceal hardware and accommodate a partial spinal rig. Beneath it, a structured collarless shirt in dark indigo — Yoruba-inspired block print barely visible in direct light — tucked into slim tapered trousers with concealed inner-thigh pockets. Footwear is a low-profile matte ankle boot, no metal hardware to trip scanners. Hands covered by thin grip-null gloves. A flat cap or structured hood — situationally deployed — completes the look. The whole outfit reads as Tier 3 from thirty meters and reveals nothing closer.
functionality: Concealed inner-thigh pockets; scanner-neutral boot hardware; longcoat cut accommodates spinal rig and concealed carry; grip-null gloves leave no biometric traces on surfaces; hood deployment takes under two seconds.
what_it_says: This person moves between worlds and belongs to none of them — which means they belong to whoever's paying.
manufacturer: Ashwall Independent (assembled from multiple unlicensed sources)
story_hooks: The block-print shirt is a specific pattern tied to a dissolved Lagos-corridor trade guild — wearing it is either a statement or a mistake.
The inner-thigh pocket contains a data chip that the wearer claims not to know the contents of.
Every piece of this outfit was purchased separately, in different districts, over eighteen months — someone built an identity that can't be traced to a single transaction.

physical_description.visual_profile: A studied exercise in deliberate anonymity. The silhouette is broad-shouldered and unremarkable—neither fashionable nor obviously worn. The longcoat hangs with intentional drape, suggesting both concealment and function. The overall impression is of someone who has learned to move through crowds without being remembered.
physical_description.fit: Longcoat is deliberately oversized through the torso and arms, tapering slightly at the hem for mobility. The collarless shirt sits flush against the body with subtle structured panels at the shoulders. Trousers are slim-tapered, cut high at the waist with a straight drop. All garments allow for layered augmentation without visible distortion.
physical_description.primary_material: Waxed synthwool blend for the longcoat (moisture-resistant, sound-dampening); dark indigo cotton-synthetic composite for the shirt (breathable, signal-neutral); recycled-polymer twill for trousers; matte ballistic-weave ankle boot with non-conductive sole.
physical_description.texture: Longcoat has a subtle waxy sheen that catches light without reflecting; textured enough to hide minor damage. Shirt features hand-block printed Yoruba geometric patterns that are almost invisible in normal light but suggest depth and cultural identity when examined closely. Trousers are smooth with a slight nap. Gloves are thin, high-grip, barely textured.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant slate-grey with charcoal undertones on the longcoat. Dark indigo shirt with faint pattern suggesting deep blues and blacks. Black trousers. Matte black boots. Gloves in dark grey or charcoal. No bright accents; no reflective elements.
physical_description.closures: Longcoat secured by hidden magnetic snaps concealed beneath the waxed fabric; no visible fasteners. Shirt is fitted, worn untucked or tucked depending on operation. Trousers feature a friction-fit waistband with internal utility tabs rather than traditional belt loops. Boots have a side zip hidden by the vamp, no laces or visible hardware.
distinctive_features: Concealed inner-thigh pockets on trousers—deep, reinforced seams, accessible through hidden slits
Waxed longcoat with subtle quilting along spine and shoulders (pressure distribution for rig support)
Non-reflective boot sole designed to avoid scanner trip-wires common in corpo zones
Grip-null gloves with embedded micro-texturing for handling delicate electronics
Optional flat cap or structured hood—both in matching slate-grey, kept in longcoat's internal stash pocket
Yoruba block-print shirt as cultural marker—visible only to those who look closely, signaling diaspora heritage
Zero visible branding, serial numbers, or manufacturer tags
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 from distance; reads as functional working-class. Closer inspection reveals thoughtful construction that suggests resources and knowledge—border between Tier 2 minimalism and Tier 3 pragmatism, deliberately ambiguous.
physical_description.cultural_context: Fixer aesthetic. Someone who moves between corporate facilities, street networks, and back-alleys without drawing attention. The Yoruba block print hints at diaspora identity but is coded enough to be missed by casual observers. Worn by information brokers, black-market augmentation facilitators, and independent operators who survive by being forgettable.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deliberately broken-in. The longcoat shows subtle creasing around movement points—elbows, shoulders, hips—but is scrupulously maintained. No visible patches or damage; wear is uniform and intentional. Everything fits like it has been worn for years, but nothing looks neglected. This is the uniform of someone who has invested in quality and disciplines their appearance as operational security.

image_prompt: A figure in slate-grey waxed-wool longcoat and indigo block-print shirt stands in three-quarter profile against a rain-slicked industrial corridor, neon signs reflecting in wet concrete. Matte ankle boots, grip-null gloves, structured hood partially raised. The longcoat settles with visible weight, concealing broad shoulders. Moody cyan and amber backlighting creates rim-light separation from the dark steel and concrete environment. Close-up inset detail shows the faint Yoruba geometric pattern barely visible on the shirt. Dark, film-noir cyberpunk aesthetic. Shot on dark mannequin or androgynous model. Emphasize the studied neutrality and functional elegance. --ar 2:3 --v 6
